findings.title: Review-reply publication is outside the existing publisher authority

RFC0015 §Immutable export before all remote effects limits PR update to title/body/fixed labels and forbids review/generic provider operations. confine-qa-publication-authority §Closed publication operations does not authorize posting or resolving inline review comments.
findings.impact: Outcome E assumes a mutation capability the separately owned adopted publisher cannot expose; implementing it would silently expand external authority.
findings.minimal_correction: Remove automated review-reply/resolve operations from this direction. Retain sanitized response drafts or operator handoff locally; follow-up publication may use only bound branch update and authorized PR metadata. Any desired comment mutation requires its own owner-adopted publisher contract change.

findings.title: Retained null-PR projection asserts a false escalation and cannot represent ambiguity consistently
findings.evidence: Proposed fix column still mandates "No PR — escalated to user." whenever pr is null. The same delta requires unknown provider outcomes to remain ambiguous and inconclusive outcomes to remain distinct. The retained proposal_state enumeration is only none/unpublished/published.
findings.impact: An ambiguous remote creation or inconclusive no-op can still render a false absence/human-handoff claim, undermining the core truthful-outcome goal.
findings.minimal_correction: Make Proposed fix column conditional on authoritative publication and diagnostic state; provide explicit ambiguous/unavailable presentation and only show escalation when operator disposition exists. Give the response an unambiguous typed representation for unknown publication (and update its consumers), preserving retained local proposals without asserting remote absence. Add this exact replacement to intentional-replacements.

findings.title: Terminal lifecycle and retention timestamps are underdefined after removing PR-open closure
findings.evidence: PR-open now keeps closed_at null, but PR merged/closed transitions do not require closed_at. Newly supported blocked_environment, already_fixed and design_required outcomes have no terminal execution-status/closed_at mapping. Retained Raw Log Retention and Cleanup exempts all linked rows whose closed_at is null; QA manifesto purges raw lines 14 days after closure.
findings.impact: A conforming implementation may leave completed investigations indefinitely active for retention, or count PR closure/publication failure as execution failure despite the separate-axis promise. Budget/admission/UI behavior would depend on worker-invented state mappings.
findings.minimal_correction: Define a compact outcome/lifecycle transition table, including whether each result closes the investigation, authoritative closed_at/merge timestamps, circuit-breaker contribution and independent recovery/publication state. Require merge and closed-without-merge to close the investigation when terminal, and ensure all completed no-PR diagnoses have an explicit closure mapping. Add scenarios proving retention after these transitions.

findings.title: Execution breaker and retained API/reset contract use incompatible event populations
findings.location: openspec/changes/restore-qa-remediation-loop/specs/qa-investigation-dispatch/spec.md:130; specs/qa-dashboard/spec.md:296-304; allocation-plan.md sections B and C
findings.evidence: The new terminal lifecycle scenario counts actual failed/timeout sessions and completed inconclusive diagnoses, resets on supported completed diagnoses, and excludes publication-only failures. The carried GET circuit-breaker and reset scenarios still derive every breaker query from only closed healing attempts after reset. PR-open is now explicitly nonterminal with closed_at unset, and follow-up sessions share an attempt. A supported patch_ready/pr_open completion cannot reset the closed-at query, and a failed follow-up on an open PR cannot enter it. Delayed PR closure can instead reintroduce an execution from before the reset.
findings.impact: Dispatch admission, summary, reset evidence and the detail chip can disagree or evaluate the wrong failure streak. Closing a PR is no longer a valid execution event boundary.
findings.minimal_correction: Define one canonical ordered breaker-event projection using trusted initial/follow-up session completion plus typed diagnostic classification, with explicit reset cutoff and unknown/blocked handling. Make every API, admission and reset-evidence consumer use it, retaining auditable reset/no-op behavior. Allocate B the producer and C only the integration consumer, or state another single owner. Add a scenario covering successful open PR, failed follow-up and late PR closure across a reset.

findings.impact: A worker preserving this carried clause must create a second credential holder outside the adopted confinement boundary, or violate the modified requirement. Read-only provider use does not remove the credential-holder contradiction.
